knowledge_point.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosine Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
The period of $y=cos⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for any integer $n$ we have

$$
cos⁡x=cos⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-3$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡x=cos⁡(x+2\cdot (-3)\cdot \pi )=cos⁡(x-6\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $cos⁡x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},$ then $cos⁡(x-6\pi )=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}4cos⁡(x-6\pi )-1 & =4(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-1 \\  & =2 \sqrt{3}-1 \\  & =-1 + 2 \sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
